title: UNDP hands SESU the Ukrainian “Mines Eye” AI aerial detection system after a pilot that scanned over 360 hectares in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts
summary: Mines Eye (magnetometry, visual/infrared imaging, AI detection of explosive remnants) scanned over 360 ha in a five-month SESU pilot; handed over 21 June 2025. No detection or land-release counts.
account: UNDP Ukraine's press release of 21 June 2025, datelined Mykolaiv, says that UNDP, with financial support from the Government of Luxembourg, “officially handed over the Mines Eye aerial detection system to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU)” at the base of SESU's Main Department in Mykolaiv oblast, in the presence of UNDP Acting Administrator Haoliang Xu. The release describes the system, “Developed in Ukraine” by a developer it does not name, as combining magnetometry with visual and infrared aerial imaging and states that “Using artificial intelligence, it detects explosive remnants of war (ERW), including anti-tank mines, even beneath vegetation”, producing maps and anomaly reports for operators before manual or mechanical clearance. Over a five-month pilot, UNDP-trained SESU teams “used the system to scan over 360 hectares of confirmed and suspected hazardous areas in Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblasts”. SESU First Deputy Head Vitalii Myroniuk is quoted that the technology “enables us to detect threats in areas that are too dangerous for manual inspection”. The release gives no number of items detected or confirmed, no hectares released, and no accuracy figure; an earlier check noted that UNDP's 26 June 2025 release concerned a testing exhibition with mock devices. No source independent of UNDP or SESU was found.
purpose: Built to survey contaminated land remotely and flag explosive remnants of war, including anti-tank mines under vegetation, so that clearance teams can plan safely; the pilot was that intended use.
system: Mines Eye aerial detection system (unmanned aerial platform with magnetometry, visual and infrared sensors, and AI detection of explosive remnants of war)
developer: Ukrainian developer not named in the UNDP release ('Developed in Ukraine')
deployer: State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU), Kharkiv and Mykolaiv oblast demining teams; procured by UNDP with funding from the Government of Luxembourg
segment: State emergency service survey of hazardous areas
taxonomy_note: No detection or land release is reported; the type names the agency's stated aim of faster survey.

ratings.reason: SESU scanned over 360 hectares with the system during the pilot; the release gives no detection counts, confirmation rates or clearance results against which to measure the benefit.
No land released to communities, casualty avoided or farmland restored is documented; the officials' statements about faster and safer demining are expectations.

ai_role.statement: UNDP's release attributes the detection of explosive remnants beneath vegetation to the system's artificial intelligence working on magnetometry and visual and infrared imagery, but reports only area scanned; no detection, false-alarm or confirmation figure is given, and no source independent of UNDP and SESU was found. The developer is unnamed, so the AI component cannot be characterized further.
